pain: Sell-side coverage of small and mid caps collapsed post-MiFID II; nobody publishes serious work on these names
v1: Two 15-page initiations a month, published on Substack behind a paywall
channel: Substack + X + network amplification, from a standing start
verdict: Ceiling gate fires: honest best case is ~£60-75k of year-one cash, not £200k. The network is excellent and pointed at the wrong buyer.

why.distribution: Can reach 30-50 analysts and PMs who will read and share, but they are not the buyer of a retail newsletter - they produce this themselves. The actual buyer requires building an audience from zero. Adjacency, not access.
why.demand: Category willingness-to-pay is proven (paid equity newsletters exist and work). Nothing specific to her: nobody has been asked, nobody has offered money.
why.fmf: The research half is a 5. The other half of the job - audience-building, retention marketing, writing for a public rather than institutional reader - is untested, and it is half the work.
why.revenue_structure: Monthly subscription, but paid-newsletter churn is brutal: 40-60% annually is normal.
why.defensibility: Voice, back catalogue and a subscriber list that compounds. Copyable, but not cheaply.
why.leverage: Real media economics. Docked one: a deep dive is 20-40 hours, so cadence is bound to her calendar and revenue stops within a quarter if she does.
why.capital: Filings free, Koyfin/TIKR ~£1k/yr, Substack takes a cut rather than a fee. Under £2k.
why.time_to_revenue: First pound is trivial and meaningless. First revenue indicating a business needs a free list of ~2,000+, which is 6-9 months.
why.tailwind: Retail participation up and the coverage gap is real, but synthesised research from public filings is the category most exposed to general-purpose models. Stage 2 of her own plan concedes this.
why.ceiling: See arithmetic - best honest case is roughly a third of the target.

ceiling_arithmetic: Substack 10% + Stripe ~3%, so she keeps ~87%. £200k net needs ~£230k gross. At £15/mo = 1,533 paying subs; at £25/mo = 920. At a 5% free-to-paid conversion that is 18,000-30,000 free subscribers within 12 months from zero, in a deliberately narrow niche - a top-1% outcome. Strong year one from a standing start is 3,000-6,000 free and 150-400 paying. Best honest case: 400 x £25/mo x 87% = £104k EXIT RUN-RATE; subscribers arrive across the year so year-one cash is roughly half that: £55-75k. Clears £200k somewhere in year three.
carries: Near-zero capital, genuine media leverage, and research quality deliverable on day one at a level almost nobody in the category can match.
kills: The buyer is a stranger. Every asset in the profile points at institutional investors; this sells to retail. The £15/mo price is the consequence, and it forces a subscriber count unreachable in a year. Fixed by changing the buyer, not by writing better - a reshape, not a repair.
test: Two weeks, £0. Message 25 named buy-side PMs and analysts from her own eight years plus hedge fund contacts via her husband, with a priced proposition: 'Independent deep-dive coverage of under-covered UK/European SMID names, two initiations a month plus model access, £1,200/month per fund, annual. Can I send you the first one free?'
test_pass: Three or more ask to see the note AND at least one takes it to a budget holder or agrees to a paid pilot - implies the 15-client base exists.
test_fail: Warm encouragement, 'send it over', and not one budget conversation. That is the 1-anchor (nice idea, you should build that) and it means the institutional path is not there.
reshape: Sell the same research to funds at £1,000-1,500/month on annual contracts; run the Substack free as top-of-funnel and credibility engine rather than as the product. Distribution 2 to 4, ceiling 2 to 4, revenue structure 4 to 5, time-to-revenue 2 to 4; leverage drops to 3 and tailwind to 2.
flags: The three stages are three different companies (media / software / regulated asset manager) and only credibility transfers. Stage 2 would eat stage 1's product. Stage 3 needs FCA authorisation or a regulatory host, plus a personal-account-dealing and disclosure policy from day one.
sources: FCA PS24/9 (Jul 2024) and PS25/4 (May 2025) restore joint payments for research and execution - see Detail row for the reshape.
